Verdict: REVISEThe PP-path identities, the local necessary-and-sufficient reserve inequality, the backward-connector obstruction, and the alternate-phase inventory are correct. I found one material scope defect: §3 invokes the global original-receiver ledger without explicitly restoring the hypotheses under which that ledger is additive. Under the note’s opening assumption of an arbitrary feasible configuration, the displayed global identity can fail because two outside endpoint components can have overlapping physical-tile receivers.This requires a small mathematical correction to the global coefficient-one paragraph. It does not affect the path contraction, equations (1)–(5), or the all-parameter neutral-family calculations.I reviewed the supplied constructions as written mathematics, using the authorized standard-elbow uniqueness/freezing dependency. I did not execute the supplied programs or verify Lean execution.1. Required revision: restrict the global receiver-ledger paragraph in §3The supplied dependency NATIVE_GUARD_COMPENSATION_AND_VIRTUAL_GUARD_OBSTRUCTION.md, §1, explicitly works with an original pair that is feasible and single-terminal. The new note begins with any feasible configuration, and §3 does not explicitly return to the stronger setting before asserting
$$\operatorname{margin}
=\sum_{\text{packets}}S_J+D_{\rm out}-q+R_{\rm out}.$$
Packet disjointness and containment of their complete receivers do not, by themselves, exclude overlaps between receivers lying entirely outside the packets.An actual counterexample to this displayed identityTake the  $8\times4$  board with rows  $0,\ldots,7$  and columns  $0,\ldots,3$ . Set  $T=\varnothing$ , and take the actual matching
$$M=
\left\{
\{(1,0),(2,0)\},
\{(3,1),(4,1)\},
\{(6,1),(6,2)\}
\right\}.$$
This configuration is feasible. Its endpoint graph has exactly three components, each consisting of one displayed matching edge.Write the original physical tiles as
$$Q_{ab}=\{2a,2a+1\}\times\{2b,2b+1\}.$$
The three component receivers are:ComponentReceiver tilesMatching edgesSelected vertices in receiverReceiver chargeFirst edge $Q_{00},Q_{10}$  $1$  $0$  $1-2(2)=-3$ Second edge $Q_{10},Q_{20}$  $1$  $0$  $1-2(2)=-3$ Third edge $Q_{30},Q_{31}$  $1$  $0$  $1-2(2)=-3$ Choose the sole packet
$$J=Q_{30}\cup Q_{31}
=\{6,7\}\times\{0,1,2,3\}.$$
It contains the complete original receiver of its component. Both other receivers lie wholly outside it, so no receiver crosses the packet boundary.Its column types are
$$\mathrm{BB},\ \mathrm{BP},\ \mathrm{BP},\ \mathrm{BB}.$$
Consequently,
$$k=t=1,\qquad L=2,\qquad \alpha=0,\qquad \beta=1,$$
and
$$S_J=\frac{8}{2}-\frac{2}{2}=3.$$
Thus the packet satisfies all the local hypotheses and satisfies (4).Outside the packet, both component charges are  $-3$ , giving
$$q=0,\qquad R_{\rm out}=6.$$
The outside endpoint-free tiles are  $Q_{01},Q_{11},Q_{21}$ . Each is blank and has deficit  $2$ , so
$$D_{\rm out}=6.$$
The asserted global right-hand side is therefore
$$3+6-0+6=15.$$
But the actual margin is
$$\frac{8\cdot4}{2}-|T|-|M|
=16-0-3
=13.$$
The discrepancy is exactly the double counting of the shared outside receiver tile  $Q_{10}$ .This is a counterexample to the unqualified global ledger equality, not to the half-area inequality. The actual margin is positive. It also does not challenge any PP-path identity.Minimal correctionIntroduce that paragraph with an explicit return to the inherited setting, for example:For the following global corollary, work in the original single-terminal receiver-ledger setting. Let the packets be disjoint unions of original physical tiles, and require every original endpoint-component receiver meeting a packet to lie wholly within that packet. Compute  $q$  and  $R_{\rm out}$  from the components outside all packets, and  $D_{\rm out}$  from the outside endpoint-free tiles.Alternatively, directly assume that the outside original component receivers are pairwise disjoint and that no outside receiver intersects a packet.The role of single terminality is concrete. If two distinct endpoint components meet one  $2\times2$  physical tile, their endpoints must occupy opposite corners: adjacent endpoints would belong to the same component. The remaining two corners cannot be endpoints, and neither can be selected, because a selection there would see both endpoints. Hence those corners are blank. Each diagonal endpoint then has occupied degree at most two, contradicting single terminality.Thus the missing assumption excludes precisely the receiver overlap used above. Full exchange freezing is unnecessary for this repair.Once the additive receiver setting is restored, the coefficient-one deduction is valid:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{margin}
&=\sum_J S_J+D_{\rm out}-q+R_{\rm out}\\
&\ge \sum_J(k_J+t_J)-q+D_{\rm out}+R_{\rm out}\\
&\ge 0.
\end{aligned}$$
Here  $D_{\rm out}\ge0$ : an endpoint-free physical  $2\times2$  tile contains at most two selections under feasibility. The resource accounting then has the required single ownership.If “the original ledger” was intended to import all the earlier theorem’s hypotheses automatically, this is a scope clarification of the intended result. It nevertheless needs to be explicit because the new note deliberately generalizes its opening framework to arbitrary feasible configurations.2. Sections 1–2: contraction, ownership, and the exact ledger are correctMultigraph classificationFor a finite region  $J$ , the degree argument is sound:A TP or BP column has one endpoint and therefore one actual matching incidence.A PP column has two endpoints and therefore two incidences.An actual matching edge inside one PP column is a loop and contributes degree two.Every matching cut has its own exterior vertex  $X$ , of degree one.There are no degree-zero vertices. A component containing a degree-one vertex is a path. A component without degree-one vertices is a finite connected degree-two multigraph and therefore a cycle.The proof handles both exceptional multigraph cases explicitly and correctly:A single PP vertex with one loop.Two PP vertices joined by two parallel matching edges.Neither can acquire an attached path without exceeding degree two.The separate exterior vertices are essential. Identifying two exterior endpoints merely because they occupy the same exterior column could join distinct accounting components. The note correctly avoids that identification.The finite-region hypothesis is implicit in the board setting and the finite counts. If §1 is intended to be completely independent of that setting, adding “finite” before “region  $J$ ” would make the scope explicit.Exact ownership and arbitrary path lengthA terminal path with  $p$  PP vertices has
$$p+2\quad\text{vertices},\qquad p+1\quad\text{actual matching edges}.$$
This includes paths with exterior terminals. For example, an  $X\!-\!X$  path through one PP column has two actual matching edges, each a cut.The endpoint-level description using auxiliary PP pairs is equivalent to the contracted description. Every original endpoint in  $J$  has one actual matching edge; every endpoint in a PP column has one auxiliary pairing incidence as well. Therefore:every original endpoint in  $J$  belongs to exactly one component;every actual matching edge meeting  $J$  belongs to exactly one component;every auxiliary PP pair belongs to exactly one component.There is no hidden duplication of matching edges, endpoints, or PP pairs. Auxiliary pairs do not supply additional matching or donor capacity.Ledger calculationThe contributions of the six column types to  $S_J$  are exactly
$$\begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}
\text{Type}&TT&BB&TP&BP&BT&PP\\ \hline
\text{Contribution}&-1&1&-\tfrac12&\tfrac12&0&0.
\end{array}$$
Hence
$$2S_J=2(B-A)+D-C=2L+D-C.$$
The terminal inventories are also exact:
$$C=2\alpha+\gamma+\tau,
\qquad
D=2\beta+\gamma+\delta.$$
Substitution gives
$$\boxed{
S_J=L+\beta-\alpha+\frac{\delta-\tau}{2}.
}$$
No path-length term or cycle term is missing. In particular:TP–TP contributes  $-1$ .BP–BP contributes  $+1$ .TP–BP contributes  $0$ .TP– $X$  contributes  $-\tfrac12$ .BP– $X$  contributes  $+\tfrac12$ . $X$ – $X$  contributes  $0$ .The cut inventory
$$\#\{\text{matching cuts}\}=2\epsilon+\tau+\delta$$
is correct. Thus an  $X\!-\!X$  path can have two boundary cuts but no terminal debit. The warning against assigning an automatic half-unit debit to every cut is justified.For matching-closed  $J$ ,
$$S_J=L+\beta-\alpha.$$
These identities require neither unique matching nor freezing. For fixed  $T,P,J$ , the signed terminal expression is invariant even if a different actual matching changes the component partition.3. Section 3: the local forest bound and exact target equivalence are correctA TT column contains two vertically adjacent selections. Each already has its one permitted occupied neighbor. Consequently the cells immediately to either side of both selections must be blank, forcing each neighboring column to be BB.The endpoint conditions exclude a TT column at either end of a band. The BB/TT graph therefore consists of alternating intervals
$$BB,TT,BB,\ldots,TT,BB,$$
including singleton BB intervals.Each component contains one more BB vertex than TT vertex. Therefore its component count is exactly  $B_i-A_i$ , and summing over bands gives  $L$ .Every band has a first BB column, so it contributes at least one component. When  $n$  is even and the final column is also BB, the two boundary columns have opposite parity. The two ends of a single alternating interval have the same parity. Thus those boundary BB columns cannot lie in the same component. Such a band contributes at least two components.Accordingly,
$$L\ge k+t.$$
Combining this with the exact terminal ledger yields
$$\begin{aligned}
S_J\ge k+t
&\iff
L+\beta-\alpha+\frac{\delta-\tau}{2}\ge k+t\\
&\iff
\boxed{
2\alpha+\tau\le 2(L-k-t+\beta)+\delta.
}
\end{aligned}$$
This is genuinely necessary and sufficient. It is not merely a sufficient estimate.For matching-closed packets, the equivalence reduces exactly to
$$\boxed{\alpha\le L-k-t+\beta.}$$
The matching-closed no-TP–TP corollary follows immediately:
$$\alpha=0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
S_J=L+\beta\ge k+t.$$
Matching closure must remain part of that class. An open packet with  $\alpha=0$  may still have TP– $X$  debits. The note states closure when introducing the class; later shorthand should continue to refer to that definition.The discussion of future allocation is also correct: the identity does not construct an injection assigning the interval reserve and BP–BP credits to TP–TP demands. Such an allocation requires an additional geometric argument with no reuse.4. Sections 4–5: the original-phase path and backward connector are correctComplete original-phase inventoryFrom the supplied construction, the matching consists of: $W/2$  upper-bar horizontal edges; $W/2-1$  lower-bar horizontal edges;one short-tip edge; $H/2$  outer right-leg edges; $H/2-1$  inner right-leg edges;one neutral-pair edge.Their total is
$$\frac W2+\left(\frac W2-1\right)+1
+\frac H2+\left(\frac H2-1\right)+1
=W+H.$$
In the original row phase, the neutral edge and short-tip edge begin the contracted path as
$$(4,5),\ (3,5),\ (2,5).$$
The alternating upper- and lower-bar matching edges then traverse every band-2 column from  $5$  through  $W+4$ . The outer right-leg matching continues through successive bands in column  $W+4$ , ending at band  $H/2+2$ .Thus the complete vertex list in (6) is correct:

(2,c)\ (5\le c\le W+4),\
(b,W+4)\ (3\le b\le H/2+2).$$

vertices and therefore

actual matching edges.Every remaining matching edge is an inner-leg vertical edge in column  $W+3$ , lying inside an original PP column. These are precisely the loops at

numbering  $H/2-1$ .The path and loops exhaust the matching:

There is exactly one terminal path, of type TP–TP. Hence

Terminal supportsAt  $(8,5)$ , the four neighboring cells are:

(8,4),(9,5)\in T,\qquad

and  $(H+4,W+3)$  is blank.Thus both terminal endpoints have precisely the two stated original selected supports.This does not extend to every interior endpoint. Therefore

S_J
&=\frac{(H+8)(W+12)}2-(H+7)-(W+H)\\
&=\frac{WH}{2}+3W+4H+41.

Since  $\alpha=1$  and  $\beta=0$ ,
$$L=S_J+1
=\frac{WH}{2}+3W+4H+42.$$
These counts can also be checked directly from the original columns: there are no TT columns, two TP columns,  $H+5$  BT columns, and  $W+H-1$  PP columns. Subtracting these from the total number of columns gives the same  $L=B$ .Connector direction and parityAt the first terminal, band  $4$ , column  $5$ :column  $4$  is BT;column  $6$  is BB.At the other terminal, band  $H/2+2$ , column  $W+4$ :column  $W+3$  is BB;column  $W+5$  is BT.There are no TT columns in this configuration, so the relevant BB intervals are singletons.Applying the stated rule—outgoing right boundary to incoming left boundary—therefore forces
$$(H/2+2,W+3)\longrightarrow(4,6).$$
Its column displacement is
$$6-(W+3)=3-W<0.$$
Moreover,  $W+3$  is odd and  $6$  is even, so it changes parity.The reflection observation is correct for a left–right reflection. Under  $c\mapsto W+11-c$ , the two BB columns become  $8$  and  $W+5$ . Reflection also exchanges their boundary roles. Reapplying the same rule gives
$$W+5\longrightarrow 8,$$
again decreasing and parity-changing.This is a valid obstruction to preservation of the specified native connector rule under arbitrary PP-path contraction. It is neither a directed cycle nor a counterexample to the packet target. The note maintains that distinction correctly.5.
